name_reason: Already matches fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=inventory accessor in battle). Descriptor accurately reflects 'return item_id of one inventory slot'. No address residue; trailing tokens are semantic words not hex.
purpose: Accessor that returns the item_id byte stored in a given inventory slot of a given runtime combatant.
logic_summary: Indexes data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[char_idx] (80-byte runtime_char stride), then reads inventory_slots[slot_idx*2 + 1]. inventory_slots[] is a 16-byte array at struct +0x0A holding 8 slots of (flag, item_id); item_id is the second byte of each 2-byte slot. asm confirms: char_idx*80 + base(0x53A45) + slot_idx*2 + 0x0B, MOVZX byte. Leading __CHK(4,...) is the Watcom bounds-check intrinsic (verified CRT-injected, not game logic).

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into the runtime_char array (which combatant). Callers pass attacker/defender/character unit indices.
params.reason: Descriptive, no address residue; matches usage across callers (attacker_idx/defender_idx/char_idx all flow in here).

params.name: slot_idx
params.semantics: Inventory slot index 0..7 (selects one of the 8 two-byte slots).
params.reason: Descriptive, no address residue; matches usage (weapon_slot / equipped-item-slot results passed in).

returns.semantics: item_id at that slot (index into item_effect_table, 215 items @ 0x602AC, 23B each). Typically passed to fd2_get_item_effect_entry. 0x80 split: 0x00..0x7F weapon/armor/item, 0x80..0xD6 spellbook.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct but terse: did not state what char_idx/slot_idx mean nor that inventory_slots starts at struct +0x0A or that flag bit 0x80 = empty.
notes: fd2-knowledge struct query shows inventory area at 0x12 in an older walkthrough/save memory-hack map; the authoritative src/include/types.h runtime_char places inventory_slots at +0x0A, which is confirmed by the disassembly (base 0x53A45, *80 stride, +0x0B load). No discrepancy in the code/src; the KB walkthrough map is a different context. __CHK is Watcom CRT bounds-check intrinsic, untouched.
